blocks.html: Anycast is a network routing technique where multiple servers around the world share the same IP address. When a user makes a request to that IP, the internet’s routing system (BGP) automatically directs the request to the nearest or best-performing server in the group.
blocks.text: Anycast is a network routing technique where multiple servers around the world share the same IP address. When a user makes a request to that IP, the internet’s routing system (BGP) automatically directs the request to the nearest or best-performing server in the group.

blocks.html: This is heavily used by CDNs and DNS providers. For example, when you hit a CDN’s API endpoint, you don’t connect to a single fixed server — instead, Anycast ensures you’re routed to the closest CDN Point of Presence (PoP), reducing latency and improving reliability.

blocks.html: In short: Anycast = one IP, many servers, user goes to nearest one.
